text:
Predicates:
SuperheroMovie(x) ::: x is a superhero movie.
GoodGuy(x) ::: x is a good guy.
BadGuy(x) ::: x is a bad guy.
Fight(x, y) ::: x fights y.
Wins(x) ::: x wins a fight.
Loses(x) ::: x loses a fight.
NamedAfter(x, y) ::: the movie x is named after character y.
Appears(x, y) ::: character x appears in movie y.
Premises:
∀x (SuperheroMovie(x) → ∀y (GoodGuy(y) ∧ Appears(y, x) → Wins(y))) ::: In superhero movies, the good guys always win.
SuperheroMovie(surprisingAdventures) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie.
∀x ∀y ((GoodGuy(x) ∧ BadGuy(y) ∧ Appears(x, surprisingAdventures) ∧ Appears(y, surprisingAdventures)) → (Fight(x, y) ∧ Fight(y, x))) ::: Good guys fight bad guys and vice versa.
Fight(sirDigby, nemesis) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
NamedAfter(surprisingAdventures, sirDigby) → GoodGuy(sirDigby) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character is a good guy.
NamedAfter(surprisingAdventures, sirDigby) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is named after Sir Digby.
∀x ∀y (Fight(x, y) ∧ Wins(x) → Loses(y)) ::: If somebody wins a fight, the person they are fighting loses.
NamedAfter(surprisingAdventures, sirDigby) → Appears(sirDigby, surprisingAdventures) ::: If a superhero movie is named after a character, that character appears in the movie.
Conclusion:
Loses(nemesis) ::: Sir Digby’s nemesis loses.
